chains.title: Null Hypothesis: No TF-mediated effect of rs642961 on IRF6 or nearby genes influencing Cleft Lip.
predictions: The variant rs642961 functions as a passenger mutation or is linked to a truly causal variant, independent of TF binding at this locus.

chains.title: A allele increases binding to SOX2, leading to protective regulatory changes in IRF6 expression.

links.claim: The ref allele (A) binds to SOX2 more strongly than the alt allele (G).
The variant is located in a highly active dELS (EH38E2863563).
The differential binding by SOX2 influences the regulatory state of IRF6.
The impact occurs within a relevant developmental cell type.
The regulatory consequence leads to an increased risk of Orofacial cleft associated with the A allele.

predictions: Increased binding affinity of the A allele (ref) for SOX2 leads to altered IRF6 regulation, consistent with E04.
falsified_if: Ref binding to SOX2 is unaffected by the A>G substitution.
The directionality of the SOX2 binding change is inconsistent across QBiC-SELEX models (E06).

chains.title: Reference allele (A) increases binding to TEAD1, disrupting developmental transcription factor activity affecting IRF6.

links.claim: The ref allele (A) binds to TEAD1 more strongly than the alt allele (G).

The binding change influences the regulatory output of IRF6.
The functional impact occurs within a relevant developmental cell type.

predictions: TEAD1 binding is increased by the A allele, leading to altered IRF6 regulation and consistent with E04.

chains.title: G allele increases binding to TFAP2B, altering developmental gene regulation leading to Cleft Lip risk (Directional Conflict).

links.claim: The alt allele (G) binds to TFAP2B more strongly than the ref allele (A).
The variant disrupts the regulatory function of the enhancer EH38E2863563, which is a dELS.
The binding change at the dELS influences the expression of the developmental gene IRF6.
The functional impact occurs within a relevant developmental cell type.
This altered regulation leads to an increased risk of Orofacial cleft (Cleft Lip) associated with the G allele.

predictions: The G allele increases TFAP2B occupancy at the enhancer, altering the regulatory output towards IRF6.
The G allele increases risk of ORAL cleft.
falsified_if: TFAP2B binding is unaffected by the A>G substitution.
IRF6 expression remains unchanged despite altered TFAP2B binding.
The effect allele for Orofacial cleft is found to be A (E04).

grades_v0.reason: E13 shows TFAP2B has an own QBiC-SELEX model and predicts alt G binds more strongly (z 23.98, effect 1.688), but this is an in vitro binding prediction only; no allele-specific reporter, EMSA, ChIP or perturbation evidence is cited.
E03 places the variant in dELS EH38E2863563, but it does not show that the A>G change disrupts enhancer activity; the z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not functional perturbation.

E02 only shows IRF6 is 9.7 kb away, and E05 provides L2G scores for IRF6 in some credible sets; neither shows that the TFAP2B binding change alters IRF6 expression. The E05 eQTL credible sets listed are for TRAF3IP3, not IRF6.
No evidence is cited for TFAP2B occupancy or IRF6 regulation in a cleft-relevant developmental cell type.

E04 reports the orofacial cleft effect allele as A, while H1 claims the G/alt allele increases TFAP2B binding and risk. This is a direction conflict, and E06 only supplies titles without quotes or functional data.

E16 shows SOX2 has an own QBiC-SELEX model and predicts alt G binds less strongly, implying ref A binds more, but this is only a binding prediction. The same group notes members disagree on direction.
E03 annotates the variant in a dELS, but does not show that the variant alters the element's regulatory activity; activity z-scores are nonspecific maxima over biosamples.
E02 gives proximity to IRF6 and E05 gives modest L2G support in the orofacial cleft set (IRF6 0.16), but there is no IRF6 eQTL or perturbation evidence connecting SOX2 binding to IRF6 expression.
No SOX2 ChIP, expression, or developmental cell-type evidence is cited.

E04 reports an orofacial cleft association with effect allele A, which is directionally consistent with H2, but the evidence is a modest genetic association and does not show that the SOX2/IRF6 regulatory mechanism causes the phenotype.

E08 shows ETV5 has an own QBiC-SELEX model and predicts alt G binds more strongly (z 77.65, effect 1.32), but this is a binding prediction only, with no direct allele-specific occupancy or reporter assay.
E03 only annotates the variant within a dELS; no evidence is cited that the variant changes enhancer function.
E02/E05 provide proximity and L2G context for IRF6, but do not show that ETV5 binding at this element regulates IRF6 expression.
No evidence is cited for ETV5 function in a relevant developmental cell type.

E04 reports the orofacial cleft effect allele as A, whereas H3 claims the G/alt allele increases ETV5 binding and contributes to cleft risk. The direction conflicts, and E04 alone does not tie ETV5 or IRF6 to the phenotype.
E10 shows TEAD1 has an own QBiC-SELEX model and predicts alt G binds less strongly, implying ref A binds more, but this is only an in vitro binding prediction.
E03 annotates the variant in a dELS, but does not demonstrate that the variant affects the enhancer's regulatory activity.
E02 and E05 provide only proximity and L2G context; there is no direct evidence that TEAD1 binding at this element changes IRF6 expression.
No TEAD1 ChIP, expression, or developmental cell-type evidence is cited.
E04 reports an orofacial cleft association with effect allele A, directionally consistent with H4, but the link from TEAD1 binding to IRF6 regulation and cleft risk is not shown.

grades_final.reason: E13 reports a QBiC-SELEX in vitro binding change for TFAP2B (effect +1.688, alt G binds more), but no allele-specific cellular or perturbation binding assay is provided; QBiC-SELEX alone is only weak support.
E03 shows the variant lies within dELS EH38E2863563, but the claim that it disrupts enhancer function is not tested by any reporter, MPRA, or perturbation assay.
E02 places IRF6 9.7 kb away and E05 gives L2G/credible-set support for IRF6, but there is no IRF6 eQTL or perturbation showing that the TFAP2B binding change alters IRF6 expression.
No cell-type evidence is cited; the QBiC-SELEX expression filter was skipped and no developmental cell type is shown.
E04 reports the Orofacial clefts association with effect allele A, not G; this directly conflicts with the H1 claim that G increases cleft risk. E06 does not provide an allele-specific direction.
E16 shows SOX2's own QBiC-SELEX model has effect -1.646 (alt G binds less, so ref A binds more), but this is in vitro binding only and the SOX group has direction disagreement among members.
E03 directly shows the variant lies within cCRE EH38E2863563, a dELS with DNase and H3K27ac activity in the ENCODE/SCREEN data.
E02 proximity and E05 L2G/credible-set data nominate IRF6, but no IRF6 expression QTL or perturbation shows that SOX2 binding at this element regulates IRF6.
No relevant developmental cell-type evidence is cited; expression context is absent and the QBiC-SELEX expression filter was skipped.

E04 reports Orofacial clefts with effect allele A, directionally consistent with H2, but it is only a GWAS association and does not show that the SOX2 regulatory consequence causes the phenotype; E06 gives no allele-specific functional result.
E08 reports ETV5 own QBiC-SELEX effect +1.32 (alt G binds more), but this is an in vitro binding prediction/assay without allele-specific cellular perturbation.
E03 directly shows the variant is located in dELS EH38E2863563, a regulatory element classification supported by ENCODE/SCREEN.
E02 and E05 provide proximity/L2G support for IRF6 as a nearby candidate, but no evidence shows that ETV5 binding changes at this element alter IRF6 expression.
No cell-type evidence is cited, and no expression-filtered QBiC-SELEX or developmental cell context is provided.
E04 reports the Orofacial clefts association with effect allele A, not G; this conflicts with the H3 claim that the G allele contributes to cleft risk. SBP associations with G are a different trait.
E10 shows TEAD1 own QBiC-SELEX effect -2.547 (alt G binds less, so ref A binds more), but QBiC-SELEX binding alone is at best weak support for the binding link.
E03 directly shows the variant lies within dELS EH38E2863563, supporting its location in a regulatory enhancer element.
E02 proximity and E05 L2G/credible sets nominate IRF6, but there is no IRF6 eQTL or perturbation linking TEAD1 binding at this element to IRF6 regulatory output.
No relevant developmental cell-type evidence is cited; no expression context or cell-type-specific epigenomic data are provided.
